subject: Order form: pricing carve-out, billing residency & tax responsibility
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acmeai.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: tom.hale@acmeai.com
Date: 2025-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form questions — billing entity & tax responsibilities

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal is reviewing the MSA and the order form; two items they flagged that will affect procurement timing:

1) Billing entity — Acme prefers invoices from our EU subsidiary (Acme EU S.A.) for purchases used by EMEA teams. Can Redwood invoice from the EU entity for EMEA spend?

2) Tax/residency evidence — procurement needs a certificate showing Redwood's VAT registration (or alternate evidence) in the jurisdiction we select.

Also, a related commercial ask: Acme would like the minimum commit split across two tranches (50% on signature / 50% after pilot). Can we reflect that phasing in the order form and show how credits would be applied if pilot scale is reduced?

Attachments: none yet — legal asked us to get you the requirements first.

Appreciate a quick note with the feasibility and what documents you need from our side.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Lang
Head of Procurement, AcmeAI
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order form questions — billing entity & tax responsibilities

Ben / Kim — forwarding Acme's asks. Quick summary and questions below.

Summary:
- Acme wants to invoice EMEA spend from their EU entity (so they'd like Redwood to invoice either to Acme EU S.A. or accept an EU billing flow).
- They need VAT/registration evidence for the selected billing entity.
- They want min commit split 50/50 (signature / post-pilot) and a credit/reserve mechanism if pilot underutilizes.

Questions for you both:
1) Kim — can Redwood issue invoices from an EU commercial entity (we have partner/marketplace entity options) or do we need Finance/legal approval to support this for a live contract? Any material billing lead time?
2) Ben — commercially, are you ok modelling a two-tranche min-commit? We should confirm: how do we handle pro-rata credits if pilot hits <50% of expected usage? Do we hold a credit reserve or refund?

I attached a draft note for sales talking points (internal) — will incorporate your guidance before sending back to Sophie.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Order form questions — billing entity & tax responsibilities

Jordan / Ben — quick finance/legal take below.

1) Billing entity: we can invoice from our EU subsidiary (Redwood EMEA Ltd) but it requires:
   - Legal sign-off for entity on the order form (standard language update)
   - Customer PO matching the legal entity name
   - Bank wiring details change (may add 5–7 business days to setup in our AR system)

2) VAT / tax evidence: we can provide VAT registration certificate and company tax residency letter. I attached an example we send to other EMEA customers.

3) Min-commit phasing: commercially acceptable to do 50/50 tranche, but we need explicit language on:
   - what triggers the second tranche (signed acceptance / pilot KPI threshold / date)
   - credit mechanics: recommend holding second tranche as a prepaid credit on account valid for 12 months; if usage < threshold, apply credit to future consumption rather than refund (clean from accounting POV).

Action items for sales/legal:
- Ben/Jordan to confirm trigger (we prefer time-based acceptance + usage KPI)
- Legal to review redline for entity amendment (I can prepare)
- Jordan to ask customer for the exact billing name and the legal PO cadence

Attachments: "Acme_tax_residency_certificate.pdf" (template)

Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@acmeai.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-02T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — billing entity & tax responsibilities

Sophie — thanks for the clear asks. Quick commercial proposal below so procurement can assess timeline impact.

Proposal:
- Billing entity: Redwood can invoice EMEA spend from Redwood EMEA Ltd. We'll reflect the entity name on the order form and provide EU VAT evidence.

- Minimum commit split: 50% due at signature (invoice on execution), 50% held as a prepaid credit and invoiced as a non-refundable credit on day 31 with a usage-based reconciliation window of 90 days. If pilot consumption < 50% of the agreed pilot target, remaining credit applied to future months for 12 months. If customer requests refund (rare), finance will need a written approved exception (we avoid cash refunds where possible).

- Net terms: standard Net45 for the upfront invoice; prepaid credit is not subject to additional net-term extension (applies on signature). Future consumption invoices follow customer's negotiated Net terms (we can consider Net60 for large enterprise but need GRC approval).

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_redline_v3.pdf (redlines highlighting entity and tranche language)

If this works, Jordan, please confirm with Sophie the billing legal name and desired PO flow. Kimberly, please confirm the AR onboarding steps and expected 5–7 day lead time so we can set customer expectations.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Enterprise AE (Mid-Market)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form questions — billing entity & tax responsibilities

Thanks Ben — that is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from our side:

1) Pilot trigger — Acme proposes the second tranche release on completion of a 30-day pilot where 3 KPIs are met (latency < 350ms P95, availability > 99.0%, and token throughput >= 70% of forecast). If the KPIs are missed, the second tranche becomes a credit per your proposal.

2) Net terms — Procurement typically needs Net60 for enterprise contracts. If Redwood can offer Net60 on consumption invoices (not necessarily upfront), that would accelerate approval. If Net60 requires GRC review, please flag and we can accept longer timelines.

3) PO name — billing should be to: Acme EU S.A., VAT BE123456789. We will send the PO once Redwood confirms EU entity and the invoice flow.

Attachments: draft_po_AcmeEU_PO_98721.pdf

Let us know if you want to do a quick call to confirm the acceptance KPIs and payment flow.

Regards,
Sophie

Sophie — appreciate the fast turnaround and the PO name. Summary + next steps below so procurement/legal have a single source of truth.

Summary of agreed items (pending legal redline):
- Billing entity: Redwood will invoice EMEA spend from Redwood EMEA Ltd. Customer PO should be issued to Acme EU S.A. (VAT BE123456789).
- Tax evidence: We will provide a VAT registration certificate and company tax residency letter. Kimberly attached a template; we'll replace with our live cert once AR completes setup.
- Min-commit: 50% at signature; 50% converted to a prepaid credit released on meeting pilot KPIs (30-day pilot, KPIs as you listed). Credit valid for 12 months; refunds require written exec approval.
- Net terms: We can make consumption invoices Net60, subject to GRC sign-off. Upfront invoice remains Net45 unless GRC approves Net60 across the board.

Action items:
- Jordan: send updated redline (Acme_OrderForm_redline_v3.pdf) and request PO. (today)
- Kimberly / Finance: complete AR onboarding for Redwood EMEA Ltd and provide VAT cert (ETA 5–7 business days).
- Legal (Redwood): perform entity amendment review and push final order form to Acme for signature.
- Sophie / Acme: confirm pilot start date and share PO when ready.

If that looks right I can schedule a 30-minute alignment call Wed (6/6) or Thu (6/7) to run through the pilot KPIs and get legal on the same page.

Thanks — Jordan
